summary: Keepalive + HTTP/2 connection reuse causing intermittent 429s under mixed bulk/realtime traffic
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using a combination of long-lived HTTP/2 connections with aggressive keepalive and high-volume background bulk uploads are seeing intermittent 429s on low-latency requests routed to the same API key. Impact appears correlated with connection reuse and the server-side token accounting window.

Impact:
- Sporadic 429 responses for realtime chat calls while large background embedding uploads are running.
- User-visible latency spikes and retry waves causing degraded UX for LuminaSearch support users.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (LuminaSearch dedicated-01) in prod-us-east.
- Traffic mix: ~30% realtime chat (short requests), 70% bulk embedding batches (multipart uploads).
- HTTP/2 enabled on client side with connection multiplexing and frequent keepalive PINGs.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a batch embed job with parallel multipart uploads (16 workers) across persistent HTTP/2 connections that reuse a small pool of connections.
2) Simultaneously start interactive chat sessions sending frequent short requests.
3) Observe 429s on chat routes after a period (~3–7 minutes) of sustained bulk activity.

Observed behavior:
- 429s include standard throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining appear to be decreasing even for chat requests.
- Console shows tenant-level quota nearing exhaustion despite dashboard reporting available credits.
- TCP connection stats show reuse with a small set of origin IPs and many concurrent streams.

Expected behavior:
- Route-level separation (realtime vs bulk) to prevent bulk background jobs from causing 429s on low-latency chat traffic when separate priority pools are configured.
- Throttle headers reflect per-route accounting for interactive routes.

Logs and artifacts provided by customer (attached links):
- tcpdump snippets and HTTP/2 stream counts (link: s3://lumina-logs/prod/keepalive-dump-2026-03-06.pcap)
- API traces: trace-2026-03-06T14-04.gz (shows correlation between PINGs and stream resets)
- Console screenshot showing tenant credits: https://lumina.example/screens/tenant-credit-dump.png
comments: Support (Maya Singh) 2026-03-07: Customer reported first seen 2026-03-06 14:00 UTC. They attached pcap and traces. Asked for initial triage and whether keepalive behavior could be counted against tenant burst credit.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-07: Acknowledged. Assigning to ingress/ratelimit owners to check token-counting for multiplexed HTTP/2 streams. Requesting sample API key and timestamped logs.
Customer (LuminaSearch - Alex Chen) 2026-03-07: Provided API key (redacted) and additional traces. Noted that reducing parallel workers reduces 429 frequency but doesn't eliminate it.

Ingress owner (Priya Kapoor) 2026-03-08: Initial check: healthchecks and PING frames are not intended to count as requests. Observed many concurrent active streams and repeated preflight-like OPTIONS calls from the uploader. Need deeper accounting checks in rate-limiter.

Rate-limiter (Ethan Boyd) 2026-03-09: Found a quota aggregation edge where connection-level attributes (client IP + connection id) were mapped to a shared token window. When many streams on same connection had rapid connect/disconnect, refill logic misattributed refill credits causing short-term overcounting for interactive routes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: HTTP/2 multiplexing + connection reuse causes background upload streams to be grouped and counted against a shared refill window leading to tenant credit depletion visible to realtime routes.
Hypothesis 2: Keepalive PINGs combined with probe endpoints are being misclassified as billable preflight requests by the ingress normalization layer (path normalization discrepancy).
Telemetry: token bucket logs show bursts aligned with upload worker start times. Refill window snapshots show transient negative Remaining values before automatic smoothing kicks in.

Reproduced in staging by simulating multiplexed HTTP/2 uploads with same API key and 12 parallel streams. Observed chat route 429s after ~5 minutes. Confirmed local repro consistent with customer report.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (applied 2026-03-09): Recommended customer reduce per-connection worker count to avoid overloading single-connection token accounting; customer applied and saw immediate reduction in 429 frequency.
Applied a rate-limiter config patch in staging to avoid counting PING and OPTIONS probe endpoints as billable requests (PR linked).

Long-term fix: rate-limiter change to separate per-route token windows when priority lanes are configured for dedicated pools. Scheduled rollout to canary next week (related PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/412).

Follow-up tasks: implement connection-fingerprint awareness to split refill accounting across routes for multiplexed connections; update docs on recommended worker-per-connection defaults for HTTP/2 clients.
workaround: Recommend isolating bulk embedding workers onto separate API key or enabling dedicated priority lane for bulk ingest. As immediate customer workaround, reduce parallel workers per connection to 4 and enable exponential backoff on embed retries.
next_steps: Coordinate canary rollout of rate-limiter patch with infra (target: 2026-03-16).
Create a short KB entry for customers about HTTP/2 connection reuse, keepalive, and worker-per-connection guidance.
Monitor LuminaSearch dedicated pool post-mitigation for 72 hours and update ticket with telemetry summary.
